transcript.purpose: The brainless components' own rhythm. Left as they set it.

body.purpose: Everything varnick draws at full weight: setup copy, problem lines, the composer.

chrome.purpose: The Surface panel's own furniture. One step down because the panel is beside the conversation rather than in it.

micro.purpose: The conditions strip and coverage codes. The quietest text in the product, for rows that report rather than say.

numeric.purpose: Any figure that updates in place. Tabular figures so it does not jitter.

components.name: Inline action
components.description: The dominant control in the product, and it is a word. Bare text in accent, no border, no background, no padding, sitting inside the sentence that explains why it exists. Presence is the state: it is rendered because snapshot.can() accepted the event, so there is no disabled treatment to design.
components.html: The agent stopped — the process exited.
components.css: .ds-sentence { color: var(--fg, #c0caf5); font: 400 13px/1.6 ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, monospace; } .ds-action { background: none; border: 0; padding: 0; font: inherit; color: var(--accent, #7dcfff); cursor: pointer; text-underline-offset: 3px; } .ds-action:hover { text-decoration: underline; } .ds-action:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid var(--accent, #7dcfff); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Choice button
components.description: Used only where a genuine choice must be made between options. Selected takes the accent border; neither state fills.
components.css: .ds-choices { display: flex; gap: 8px; } .ds-choice { padding: 6px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--rule, #2c2e40); border-radius: 0; background: var(--ground, #1a1b26); color: var(--fg-dim, #8b8fa3); font: 400 13px/1.6 ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, monospace; cursor: pointer; } .ds-choice--on { border-color: var(--accent, #7dcfff); color: var(--fg, #c0caf5); } .ds-choice:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid var(--accent, #7dcfff); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secret field
components.description: Takes a credential once. The value is cleared the moment it is sent and never echoed.
components.html: <input class="ds-field" type="password" placeholder="Paste the token from `claude setup-token`" />
components.css: .ds-field { width: 100%; padding: 6px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--rule, #2c2e40); border-radius: 0; background: var(--ground, #1a1b26); color: var(--fg, #c0caf5); font: 400 13px/1.6 ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, monospace; caret-color: var(--accent, #7dcfff); } .ds-field::placeholder { color: var(--fg-faint, #565f89); } .ds-field:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid var(--accent, #7dcfff); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Panel
components.description: The only surface that sits forward of the field. Raised by tone and a hairline, never by shadow.
components.html: This is a Surface, and it is yours. Ask the agent for what this should be instead.
components.css: .ds-panel { padding: 12px; border: 1px solid var(--rule, #2c2e40); border-radius: 0; background: var(--ground-raised, #1f2030); color: var(--fg-dim, #8b8fa3); font: 400 13px/1.6 ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, monospace; }

components.name: Problem line
components.description: The product's way of saying something did not happen: a mark in bad, the sentence, then an inline action if there is one thing to do about it. Never present without either a next action or an explanation of why there is none.
components.html: ✗ The sandbox could not be established. The agent will not run unconfined.
components.css: .ds-problem { color: var(--bad, #f7768e); font: 400 13px/1.6 ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, monospace; } .ds-action { background: none; border: 0; padding: 0; font: inherit; color: var(--accent, #7dcfff); cursor: pointer; text-underline-offset: 3px; } .ds-action:hover { text-decoration: underline; } .ds-action:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid var(--accent, #7dcfff); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Seeded admission
components.description: The one component whose job is to reduce trust in what is beside it. Gates on the run being seeded and on nothing else.
components.html: <button class="ds-admission">seeded data — nothing here is measured</button>
components.css: .ds-admission { background: none; border: 0; padding: 0; font: 400 13px/1.6 ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, monospace; color: var(--warn, #e0af68); cursor: pointer; } .ds-admission:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid var(--accent, #7dcfff); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
A terminal that grew a housing. The transcript at the centre is a faithful Claude Code session — the same messages, tool calls and composer a developer already recognises — and everything varnick draws around it is instrumentation: a strip that reports what the machines think, a setup screen for the one thing that must be supplied, a panel for whatever the developer built. The housing never competes with the instrument it houses.

This is why the surface is monospace throughout, flat throughout, and square throughout. Not minimalism as taste — a panel is legible because nothing on it is styled for attention. Depth is carried by two greys, `ground` and `ground-raised`, in the way a recessed bezel is darker than the face around it. There is no motion anywhere in the product, because motion in a transcript reads as something happening, and the only things happening are the ones the machines report.

The palette was not chosen. It was read off the transcript components so the application and the session it holds are one surface rather than two, and that provenance is a constraint rather than a fact about the past — see The Inherited Palette Rule. What the product refuses is equally load-bearing: it is not a dashboard of invented numbers, and it is not themeable.
keyCharacteristics: Monospace only; 13px ceiling with two quieter steps for chrome
No shadows, no motion, no radius — depth is tonal, state is textual
Colour is semantic and rare; most of the screen is three greys
Controls are text, and exist only when the machine accepts the event
Full-width shell; only prose is capped, at 110ch

rules.name: The Inherited Palette Rule
rules.body: Every value was read off the transcript components rather than chosen, so the application and the session are one surface. A new colour must already exist in the transcript or it does not ship.

rules.name: The Three Greys Rule
rules.body: If a screen is using more than ground, ground-raised and rule for structure, the structure is wrong. Colour is for meaning, not for arranging things.

rules.name: The Quiet Chrome Rule
rules.body: 13px is the ceiling and the transcript owns it. Anything varnick draws around the conversation steps down — 12px for panel furniture, 11.5px for reporting rows — and nothing steps up. #/states is the named exception: 15px title, 11px timestamps, on a coverage surface the product does not present.

rules.name: The Wide Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose caps at 110ch, not the 65ch an essay wants. A transcript is interleaved with tool output, diffs and absolute paths that must not wrap.

rules.name: The Tonal Depth Rule
rules.body: Two greys and a hairline are the entire depth vocabulary. If that is not enough separation, the layout is wrong rather than the elevation.

rules.name: The Still Surface Rule
rules.body: Nothing moves that the machines did not move. Streaming text arriving is motion the product is reporting; everything else would be motion the product is performing.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: No border-radius on anything varnick draws. A rounded corner makes an element read as an object placed on the surface; here every element is the surface.

dos: Do take every new colour from the transcript components. If it is not already in the session, it is not in the product (The Inherited Palette Rule).
Do express hierarchy with colour and position, keeping 13px as the ceiling and stepping down for chrome (The Quiet Chrome Rule).
Do render a control only when the machine accepts the event, and let its presence be the affordance — no disabled states to style.
Do cap prose at 110ch per block, and let tool output, diffs and paths run full width (The Wide Measure Rule).
Do carry depth with ground-raised plus a 1px rule border, and nothing else (The Tonal Depth Rule).
Do apply [data-numeric] to any figure that updates in place, so it does not jitter.
donts: Don't add box-shadow, a transition, an animation or an easing token. Nothing moves that the machines did not move (The Still Surface Rule).
Don't add border-radius to anything varnick draws (The Square Corner Rule).

Don't show a number the product did not measure — no status pills, health dots, sparklines or usage figures without a live reading behind them. A strip that could never populate was cut for exactly this.
Don't add a light mode, a theme switcher or a configurable palette. One world, inherited from the transcript; a clone that wants another edits the tokens.
Don't introduce a second font family, and don't add a size above 13px to anything the product presents.
Don't style varnick's chrome louder than the transcript it surrounds.
